title: ElastiCache, MemoryDB & Caching Strategies
summary: Cache hot reads, store sessions and run leaderboards in memory, and choose the caching pattern.
tldr: **ElastiCache** (Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) offloads repeated reads from RDS or Aurora, holds shared session state, and runs leaderboards with **sorted sets**.

**Lazy loading** caches only what's requested (stale until TTL). **Write-through** updates the cache on every write (always fresh, can fill with unread data). Combine write-through **with a TTL** for fresh, lean caches.
Need the in-memory store to be the **durable primary database** (no data loss)? Pick **MemoryDB**, which commits writes to a Multi-AZ transaction log. ElastiCache is a cache.

keyFacts.text: Typical ElastiCache read latency. Repeated SELECTs served from cache cut database CPU and let you avoid scaling the DB up.
**ElastiCache Serverless** scales memory and compute automatically with no node sizing, for Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached. Good fit for unpredictable traffic.
Valkey/Redis OSS **sorted sets** keep members ranked by score, so "top 100" and "my rank" are single fast commands.
**MemoryDB** persists every write to a distributed transaction log across AZs before acknowledging, giving durability with microsecond reads.
Simple, multithreaded cache with no replication, persistence or Multi-AZ failover. Choose Valkey/Redis OSS when you need any of those.

rows: Lazy loading (cache-aside)
Read cache; on miss read DB and populate
Stale data until TTL; first read is a miss
Read-heavy, some staleness is OK, cache only what's used
Write-through

Caches data that may never be read
Reads must reflect the latest write without a miss
Write-through + TTL
Fresh on write, unread entries expire
More write work
Fresh data and a cache that doesn't bloat

keywords.answer: Replica in another AZ with Multi-AZ automatic failover

traps: ElastiCache is not a durable system of record; replication and snapshots can still lose recent writes. Use MemoryDB for that.
DAX works only with DynamoDB, so it can't cache an RDS or Aurora database.
Raising the TTL to 24 hours increases hits but makes stale data worse.
A `noeviction` policy makes writes fail when memory is full; it doesn't keep the cache fresh.
Adding read replicas spreads read load but doesn't fix stale data from lazy loading.
